title: Context-anchored rolling-slab sampling for per-domain calibration bundles
creator: Sara Klein
description:
Goal: define and implement a reproducible dataset curation and sampling strategy we call 'rolling-slab with context anchors' to build per-domain calibration bundles used for FP8/INT8 quantization and accuracy validation. These bundles must reflect production prompt distributions (temporal recency, length/seq distribution, semantic cluster coverage, and tenant-weighted signal) while preserving contiguous context windows for multi-turn prompts, and must be small enough to run offline quant calibration + accuracy validation end-to-end within CI budgets (~50-200k tokens per bundle depending on domain).

Key ideas: combine a bounded sliding 'slab' window (captures recent traffic), per-domain reservoir sampling for long-tail retention, and explicit exemplar anchors to preserve rare but high-risk contexts. Stratify by semantic clusters (embedding-based k-means with adaptive k), sequence length buckets, and customer tier. Introduce a temporal decay factor (alpha) to bias newer examples in the slab while reservoir keeps historical exemplars. Ensure deterministic sampling by hashing request fingerprint + epoch seed and recording provenance metadata for reproducibility.

Deliverables: a sampling library (python) integrated with our offline data pipeline, a per-domain calibration bundle schema (JSON manifest), CI job that runs FP8 and INT8 calib+inference on representative model variants, and an evaluation dashboard with acceptance gates.

Constraints/Non-goals: we are not building a live streaming sampler; this is offline curation for calibration/validation. We will not store user PII in bundles; privacy filters and redaction are mandatory and handled by the data-prep step.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible sampler implementation (python) that generates a per-domain bundle manifest and S3 artifact path given domain name and seed
Per-domain bundle token counts configurable; default target = 100k tokens for medium domains, configurable 50k-200k
Sampling preserves contiguous context windows up to domain-configured max_context (default 2048 tokens) and does not truncate turns mid-message
Coverage metrics: for evaluated domains, semantic cluster coverage >= 80% of active clusters, sequence-length distribution KL divergence < 0.05 vs production distribution
Calibration validation: for a baseline FP32 run vs FP8/INT8 calibration pipeline, aggregate delta in log-prob (NLL) < 0.02 and top-1 token error increase < 0.5% on the bundle holdout
End-to-end CI run (sampling -> calibration -> evaluation) completes within budgeted runtime (<= 3 hours for default bundle) for chosen infra
Provenance metadata written for every bundle: domain, seed, time-range, cluster config, filters applied, and linking to source data query
Documentation and a migration guide for adding new domains and tuning slab/reservoir parameters
tasks: Design sampling specification doc with formulas for slab size, decay alpha, reservoir capacity, and anchor selection heuristic
Implement sampling library + unit tests (deterministic sampling, context preservation)
Add privacy/redaction hooks and test on synthetic PII-laden traces
Build per-domain config schema (max_context, token_targets, cluster_k heuristic, customer_weights)
Integrate sampler with offline data ETL to produce S3 bundle artifacts and JSON manifest
Hook bundles into quantization CI job and run baseline FP32 vs FP8/INT8 flows
Create dashboard panels for coverage metrics, sequence-length distribution, cluster histograms, and calibration regression alerts
Run smoke validation for 10 high-volume and 10 low-volume domains and iterate parameters
comments: 2026-03-02 Sara Klein: Kickoff meeting notes attached to Confluence. Agreed slab default = 7 days, reservoir cap default = 5k exemplars per domain. Need to validate these defaults on low-volume domains.
2026-03-04 Arjun Patel: Implemented initial deterministic hash-based seeding and context-preserving chunker. Pushed first unit tests to feature branch. Pending privacy hook integration.
2026-03-07 Lina Morales (ProdML): Reviewed cluster stratification idea; suggested using a two-stage clustering: coarse embedding k-means followed by silhouette-based split for rare topic discovery.
2026-03-09 Kai Zhang (Runtime): Pointed out CI runtime limit. Recommend early stopping in quant calibration if NLL delta exceeds 0.1 to reduce wasted runs. Will add safeguard in CI job.
2026-03-11 Arjun Patel: Ran smoke on three domains. Observed sequence-length KL at ~0.06 for one domain; adjusted bucket boundaries improved KL to 0.03. Added bucket tuning to tasks.
2026-03-12 Product review: PM approves approach but requests explicit per-tenant exclusion list (legal/opt-outs) and a clear rollback plan if calibration shows regressions on customer-facing metrics.
notes: Sampling math: slab_window_size S (in time) + reservoir R (count). For each incoming example in slab: weight = exp(-alpha * age_seconds). Reservoir keeps top-N fingerprints by combined score = rarity_score * tier_weight + uniform tie-breaker.
Anchor selection: pick up to M exemplars per semantic cluster with highest downstream risk score (derived from previous mismatch signals and human-labeled failure examples).
Privacy: run redaction lambda that replaces email/SSN-like tokens and marks examples with PII in manifest (excluded unless explicit opt-in).

Evaluation metrics: NLL delta, top-k token error delta, semantic similarity (SBERT) to FP32 outputs, longest-common-subsequence ratio for structured outputs, and a 'regression count' threshold for human review.
